title: Sources in private and public enterprises

blocks.heading: Sources in private and public enterprises
blocks.text: Internal finance arises within an existing business, especially retained profit available for use and proceeds from selling surplus assets. External finance comes from outside it: owner contributions, new share capital where the form permits, loans, overdrafts, supplier credit, leasing or grants subject to eligibility and conditions. Owner savings introduced into the enterprise are external to it, even when an owner regards the savings as personal internal funds. A loan gives funds now with repayment and interest obligations; an overdraft allows an agreed temporary negative bank balance; trade credit postpones payment to suppliers. Leasing provides use of an asset in return for payments rather than ownership through an outright purchase. A grant may support a specified purpose without ordinary loan repayment, but conditions and availability matter. Private businesses can use sources appropriate to their form. Public enterprises can retain earnings, borrow where permitted or receive state capital and allocations. The state itself obtains revenue through taxation and other public receipts and may borrow to fund expenditure. Public/private describes ownership sector; internal/external describes the origin of funds relative to the particular enterprise.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Assume fictional state-owned Temo Water retains a cash surplus and also receives an additional state capital allocation. A privately owned workshop obtains a bank loan. Temo’s retained funds are internal to its enterprise, while the new state contribution comes from outside it. The workshop’s loan is external private-enterprise finance. A public organisation can therefore have both internal and external sources; private does not mean internal.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain the two classifications. Assume fictional state-owned Oru Water finances repairs partly from retained earnings and partly from a new bank loan.

Oru is public sector because the state owns it. Retained earnings are an internal source relative to Oru, whereas the new bank loan is external to it. Both sources finance a public enterprise. Internal/external identifies where money originates relative to that enterprise; public/private identifies ownership. Neither classification replaces the other.
